chained_run_id.description: The run a `TriggerDagOperator`'s attempt started (no worker runs it).

oneOf.description: Its cleanup; none for a task without one.

core_dumped.description: Whether its process dumped core (ended by a signal).

duration_ms.description:
How long it ran, measured by the worker (the timestamps come from the master's wall
clock, so don't subtract them); none while it runs or for attempts ended by the master.

error_summary.description: The structured error summary (exception, message, traceback).

peak_memory_bytes.description:
The peak memory of its processes, sampled by the worker (about once a second); none
when it wasn't measured.

start_method.description:
How the worker started it: `spawn` (a new process: an interpreter for a Python task,
the command for a command task) or `fork` (from the fork server); none until the
worker reported its start.

status.description: How it ended (`success`, `failed`, `timed_out`, ...); none while it runs.

BackfillRequest.description:
A backfill to create (`schedr runs backfill`, decisions 363, 364, 400-404): a run per fire
time of `[from, to]` with no successful, queued or running run, oldest first.

all.description: A run for every fire time of the range, not only the missing ones (`--all`).

dry_run.description: Count only: the command's result says what would be created, and nothing is.

params.description: Values for every run's parameters, as JSON, over the DAG's defaults; checked once.

to.description: Its last moment (inclusive); now if not given, and a later one ends at now.

queued.description: Waiting for `max_active_runs`, behind the other kinds of runs.

all.description: Whether every fire time got a run (`--all`).

backfill_id.description: Its ID (the command's that created it).

created_runs.description: How many of them got a run; the others were skipped.

fire_times.description: The fire times of its range.

to.description: Its last moment (now, when it was asked for one later).

unfinished.description: Whether some of its runs are queued or running: what cancelling it would cancel.

CheckConnectionsRequest.description: Connections to check on a worker (`schedr connections check`).

name.description: One connection; all of the root's if not given.

root.description: The root; every root with connections if not given.

worker.description: The worker to run it on; one the master picks if not given.

duration_ms.description: How long its tries ran, measured by the worker.

error_kind.description: The error kind of its last failed try.

error_summary.description: The structured error summary of its last failed try.

handles.description:
The handles the attempt registered (`{"handle_type": ..., "value": ...}`), masked, in
order.

moves.description: How many times it moved to another worker (`cleanup_anywhere`).

result.description: How it ended (`ok`, `failed`, `worker_lost`, `not_needed`); none until it has.

CommandView.description: A command: an action the master applies, then marks `applied` or `rejected`.

command_id.description: Its ID; poll `GET /api/v1/commands/{command_id}` for the decision.

result.description: What it produced when applied, e.g. `{"run_id": ...}` for a trigger.

ConnectionInfo.description: A connection, as its root's current parse records it.

file.description: The file defining it, relative to the root.

refused.description: Why it can't be used: defined twice, invalid, or defined nowhere (a task declares it).

type.description:
A typed connection's type (`http`, `ssh`, `mongo`, `sql`, `generic`); none for a
`@connection` function, or one that can't be used.

used_by.description: The DAGs whose tasks declare it, by DAG.

ConnectionList.description:
Each DAG root's connections, in its current code (decision 211): what the UI lists, never
a value.

ConnectionUse.description: The tasks of one DAG declaring a connection.

tasks.description: Its tasks declaring it, in the DAG's order.

dags.description: Every DAG not removed, in ID order.

conflict.description: Every place defining it, while it is in conflict (then it can't run).

oneOf.description:
Why it is held, while its file fails to import in its root's current code (decision
72): the scheduler creates no runs of it and manual triggers are refused until it
imports again. Not set for a timeout or a runner that died (the file is parsed again).

limits.description:
The concurrency limits its current version sets, each with how many run now (decision
96): only on one DAG's view (`GET /api/v1/dags/{dag_id}`), not in the list.

oneOf.description: Where its current version is defined (none for a DAG only ever seen in conflict).

params.description:
The run parameters its current version takes, as the UI's trigger form shows them
(decision 149): only on one DAG's view, not in the list; none when it takes none.

trigger.description: Its trigger as in DAG JSON.

oneOf.description:
Its trigger's switch (decision 459): `paused` or `active`; `null` without a trigger (it
runs only when started by hand).

warnings.description:
What is wrong with its current version that shows only when a run reaches it: a
connection a task declares that its root's current files don't define, or define twice
(decision 179). Only on one DAG's view, not in the list.

DeploymentView.description:
The deployment this webserver serves, as nodes (decisions 121-123): its own, its masters
(leader and standbys) and its workers, each with its effective configuration, masked by the
node itself before it left its process (no secret in clear).

masters.description: The masters heard from lately: the leader (the lease's holder) first.

user.description:
Who this request was made as, as the webserver sees it (`anonymous` without
authentication; the person the web UI passed on, from the UI).

webserver.description: The webserver answering (one of the deployment's, if it has several).

workers.description: Every worker the master has seen, gone ones included.

at.description: When it happened, if it said.

data.description: Its data, JSON of any kind.

HeldView.description:
Why a DAG is held: its file's import error. The error is the **file's**, so every DAG of
the file is held (decision 72.3).

exception.description: The error's exception class name, e.g. `ModuleNotFoundError`.

path.description: The file, relative to its root.

reason.description:
What happened and what to do, for people: that the file failed (not only this DAG),
why, and how to fix it.

ImportErrorList.description: The import errors of each DAG root's current code.

ImportErrorView.description: A file of a DAG root's current code that failed to import (decision 66).

content_hash.description: The root's content hash that was parsed.

exception.description:
The exception's class name (`ParseTimeout`, `RunnerDied` or `ParseResultTooLarge` when
the worker stopped the file; `InvalidDag` when the master refused a DAG).

master_id.description: The master that stored the parse; none when not known (stored before it was kept).

path.description: The file, relative to the root.

LimitView.description:
A concurrency limit and how many of what it limits run now: open attempts (assigned, not
yet started, running, cleaning up), as the master counts them.

running.description:
How many run now: the DAG's tasks, the task's instances across runs, or, for
`max_active_per_run`, the most in any one run.

task_id.description: The task it is set on; none for `max_active_tasks` (the DAG's).

path.description: The file, relative to the root.

LogChunk.description: A part of an attempt's log, read from the worker that ran it.

content.description:
The log's text, whole lines only (a running attempt's last line once it ends), with
its secrets masked: a password in an address, a value after a name like `password=`
(invalid UTF-8 replaced by `U+FFFD`). A line longer than the part asked for is shown
to its last whitespace in it, then `… (the rest of this line is not shown: it is over
N bytes)`, its rest passed over.

from.description:
The first byte of `content`: the one asked for, or past it, at the start of the next
line, when that one is inside a line.

next.description:
Where the next part starts: the byte after `content`, or past it, after the part of
a line longer than a part that isn't shown.

running.description: Whether the attempt still runs (its log may grow).

size.description: The log's size when it was read.

worker_id.description: The worker it ran on (and that answered).

allOf.description: Where it runs, and its configuration.

heard_at.description: When it was last heard from (it writes its row every 10 s).

master_id.description: Its ID: the lease holder it takes the lease as.

problems.description:
Its problems as it last wrote them: its lease renewed late, a round failing, its
command notifications failing.

MasterView.description: A master, leading or standing by.

NamedEventView.description: An event posted through the API.

data.description: Its data, masked as an output is.

process_id.description: The process (shared by a master and a worker in standalone).

OutputView.description: A task's stored output in a run.

outcome.description: The outcome the task finished with.

value.description:
The value it returned, masked (decision 131: its texts' secrets, and a field whose
name has a word naming a secret); downstream tasks get it as stored.

ParamFieldView.description: One field of a DAG's run parameters, as a form shows it.

choices.description: A `choice`'s values, as JSON (strings, numbers, booleans; `null` is `nullable`).

default.description:
Its default as JSON, the form's starting value (`null` is a default); absent when it
has none or it is withheld.

name.description: The field's name, as a trigger's values name it.

nullable.description: Whether it may be `null` (`T | None`): the form has a "none" box beside it.

required.description: Whether a trigger must give it (it has no default).

secret.description:
Whether its default and choices are withheld (decision 150): its name has a word naming
a secret, or its default or a choice holds one. The form gives it an empty password
input; left empty, the master uses the default.

cancel_runs.description: Also cancel its queued and running runs.

at.description: When it happened; now if not given. A run it starts is planned for it.

data.description: Its data, JSON of any kind; `null` if not given.

key.description: Its key: a trigger starts one run per key, a waiting step matches its own key.

name.description: Its name, written as a DAG ID is.

ProblemView.description:
A problem a node has now (decision 129): shown on its node, yellow for a warning, red for
an error.

ResourceView.description: A resource of a run: its setup, its cleanup and its users.

blocking.description: Whether what follows its group waits for its cleanup.

setup.description: Its name: its setup's task ID.

state.description:
`setting_up`, `waiting_for_users`, `cleaning_up`, `cleaned`, `cleanup_failed`,
`cleanup_cancelled` (cancelled by hand: what the setup made may be left) or `not_needed`.

users.description: The tasks that use it, in the DAG's order.

connections.description: By name: those its files define, and those its tasks declare without one.

RunBackfillView.description: A backfill run's backfill and its place among the backfill's runs, oldest first.

total.description: How many runs the backfill has.

code_hashes.description:
The code hashes its attempts ran with, in the order first used. More than one: its
tasks ran on different code (it changed during the run).

params.description:
Its parameters as JSON, masked like a task's output (decision 134); `{}` for a DAG
that takes none.

resources.description: Its resources, in the DAG's order (decision 275: each one's state from its two tasks).

tasks.description: Its tasks, in task ID order.

runs.description:
Newest first: a DAG's by `planned_for`; the list over every DAG by `triggered_at`, then
run ID.

oneOf.description: Its backfill and its place in it, for a `backfill` run (`backfill 3/31`).

late_failure.description:
A `success` that learnt of a failure after its end, shown yellow (decision 309): why,
`late_cleanup_failed` for now.

parent_run_id.description:
The run whose `TriggerDagOperator` started it, for a `chained` run, or whose success
started it, for a run of a `RunOf` trigger.

since.description: The start of its window, `(since, planned_for]`.

triggered_by.description: `scheduler`, a user name, the parent run, or `trigger`.

SensorView.description: A wait step switched off for getting its host killed too many times in a row (decision 338).

strikes.description: Its host kills in a row.

cleanup.description:
How its cleanups ended (`ok`, `failed`, `worker_lost`, `not_needed`): the last, unless
one failed; none for a task without a cleanup, or before its first one ends.

instances.description:
A mapped task as a whole: how many instances it has (0 before it expands, or for an
empty list); `null` for an unmapped task and for an instance.

map_index.description:
Which instance of a mapped task, from 0; -1 for an unmapped task, and for a mapped
task as a whole (decision 80).

reason.description:
Why it waits or can't be scheduled, or why a mapped task failed without an attempt
(too many instances, a mapped value that isn't a list).

TestConnectionRequest.description: A connection to test on a worker (`schedr connections test`).

root.description: Its root; the one root defining it if not given.

timeout_ms.description: How long it may take, in milliseconds: `[webserver] connection_test_timeout` if not given.

worker.description: The worker to run it on; one the master picks if not given.

event.description: For a DAG a trigger starts: the key of an event it found, to run again.

event_at.description: And when it happened; the run's moment otherwise.

event_data.description: And its data, as JSON of any kind.

event_key.description: Or an event given here: its key. It is never stored as an event.

params.description:
Values for the run's parameters, as JSON (`{"region": "us"}`), over the DAG's
defaults; checked by the master against the DAG's schema (decision 133).

planned_for.description: The moment the run is for (`--for`); now if not given. Must not be in the future.

bookmark.description: The last key acted on: what it starts from.

called_for.description:
`@trigger(wait_for=...)` (decision 353): the run of the other DAG it is called for and
hasn't ended well with yet; `schedr triggers skip` passes it.

last_poked_at.description: When a poke's call last ended.

last_restart_at.description: When it was last started again for finding nothing for its `restart_if_idle`.

not_before.description: Not started again before this moment.

started_at.description: When this run of it started.

state.description:
`running`, `waiting` (for a free watcher slot or to start again), `stopped` (see
`stopped_why`), `switched_off` or `paused` (its DAG's, or outside its `start` and `end`).

stopped_why.description: Why it isn't running although its DAG wants it: `back_pressure` or `returned`.

stuck.description:
A running poke trigger none of whose calls has ended for over three times its `every`
plus a heartbeat: its worker may hang; `schedr triggers restart` starts it again.

involuntary_context_switches.description: Times it was preempted; none as for `voluntary_context_switches`.

peak_rss_bytes.description:
The peak resident set size, in bytes; for a forked process it includes the pages it
shares with the fork server (`peak_memory_bytes`, the watchdog's PSS, doesn't); none
for a spawned process (its memory is gone when the worker reads it).

system_cpu_micros.description: CPU time in the kernel, in microseconds.

user_cpu_micros.description: CPU time in user mode, in microseconds.

voluntary_context_switches.description:
Times it gave up the CPU (waiting for I/O or a lock), with its threads and reaped
children; none for a spawned process (only its leader thread's could be read).

interpreter.description: The interpreter it concerns; empty if none.

WatcherHostView.description: A process running a worker's wait steps, or a code set whose hosts were lost.

code.description: The code it runs: its folders' names, the copies' hashes.

hosts_lost.description: Hosts of this code lost since the agent started: crashes and memory kills.

threads.description: Its process's threads, the wait steps' among them.

tied_threads.description:
Those a wait step is tied to: running its `to_thread` calls, or started by it. The rest
of the process, a library's pools among them, can't be told apart.

wait_steps.description: The wait steps on it (none: no host runs this code now).

workers.description: Every worker the master has seen, in ID order.

WorkerNodeView.description: A worker as a node of the deployment.

config.description: Its effective configuration, masked; none from an older agent.

master_id.description: The master it registered with last; none from an older agent.

problems.description:
Its problems now: lost or offline (errors), what it reports wrong, the import errors
of files it parsed (warnings).

process_id.description: The process it runs in; none from an older agent.

WorkerView.description: A worker in the registry (kept after it is gone, so its logs can be found).

drained.description: Drained for maintenance (`schedr workers drain`): no new tasks until resumed.

incarnation_id.description: The incarnation of its agent process it last registered with.

last_heartbeat_at.description: The last sign of life the master recorded (at most once per heartbeat interval).

log_endpoint.description: Where its log endpoint listens (where a gone worker's logs were served).

master_id.description:
The master it registered with last (a master's ID, as on `GET /api/v1/deployment`):
kept while it is disconnected; none from an older agent's registration.

offline_at.description: When it went offline or was lost.

warnings.description: What is wrong with it now, as it last reported (e.g. a disabled fork server).

watcher_hosts.description:
The processes running its wait steps, as its last heartbeat said (decision 343), and
code sets whose hosts were lost.

bearer.description: A token for a mesh or proxy in front of schedr that requires one; schedr itself checks none.

get.summary:

a runner that died holds nothing: the file is parsed again (72.2). Fixing the file and
syncing the root makes the entry go.
